documents.title: Doc 59 - Infringement - Car 1 - Alleged driving erratically
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 1 - Alleged driving erratically

details.fact: Driving erratically under Safety Car conditions.
details.infringement: Breach of Articles B5.13.2a of the FIA F1 Regulations and Appendix L, Chapter IV, Articles 2 e) of the International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Driver: Reprimand (Driving). This is the driver’s 1st reprimand of the season.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 1 (Lando Norris), the team representative and reviewed video and in-car video evidence. While following the Safety Car, NOR approached Turn 1 behind a group of cars. Car 63 (George Russell) had stopped with a mechanical problem ahead of Turn 1, which caused the cars ahead of NOR to slow down. NOR explained that, due to the low sun and resulting visibility conditions, it was difficult to recognise that the cars ahead had started to slow earlier than would normally have been expected. NOR consequently misjudged his closing speed and approached the cars ahead too quickly. When he realised this, he braked heavily and deliberately steered to the left, onto the kerbs and then into the gravel bed in order to avoid contact with the cars ahead. By driving onto the kerbs, NOR had reduced grip available for braking, which further limited his ability to slow the car. In doing so, NOR momentarily overshot Car 81 (Oscar Piastri), who was directly ahead of him. The Stewards considered whether this constituted an overtake while the Safety Car was deployed. Although NOR momentarily moved ahead of PIA, this occurred solely as a consequence of NOR leaving the track while taking avoiding action. PIA immediately repassed NOR while NOR was off the track. The Stewards therefore determined that this did not constitute an overtaking manoeuvre and take no further action in respect of this aspect of the incident. The Stewards also considered that, particularly while driving behind the Safety Car, NOR should have managed the gap to the cars ahead and his closing speed with greater care. The prevailing visibility conditions were circumstances which NOR should have taken into account when determining an appropriate speed and gap to the cars ahead, rather than a reason which excused the resulting driving. The need for heavy braking and an avoiding manoeuvre into the gravel demonstrated that NOR had not maintained an appropriate margin in the circumstances. The Stewards therefore determined that NOR had driven erratically in breach of Article B5.13.2a of the FIA F1 Regulations. Such a situation should not arise while driving behind the Safety Car, and NOR was required to maintain a sufficient margin to the cars ahead. However, taking into account that NOR reacted promptly once he recognised the situation and successfully avoided contact, the Stewards consider a Reprimand as appropriate. The Stewards separately considered NOR's return to the track. Although Car 18 (Lance Stroll) was in relative close proximity, NOR returned progressively and without requiring STR to take avoiding action or otherwise creating an unsafe situation. The Stewards therefore determined that the re-join was safe. The Stewards also reviewed whether, after having re-joined the track, NOR had overtaken STR while the Safety Car was deployed. The video evidence showed that, as NOR returned from the gravel, he had already crossed the white line with at least one wheel and, as such, was back on track. At this point, he was ahead of STR and at no point did NOR pass STR. Rather, STR approached NOR while NOR was already in the process of returning to the track. The Stewards therefore determined that NOR had not overtaken STR under Safety Car conditions and as such also take no further action for this part of the incident. Accordingly, the Stewards impose a Reprimand on NOR for erratic driving. No further action is taken in relation to the re-join or the alleged overtake while the Safety Car was deployed.

documents.title: Doc 58 - Infringement - Car 27 - Unsafe release
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 27 - Unsafe release

details.fact: Unsafe act during the pit stop resulting in an unsafe situation.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: The competitor (Audi Revolut F1 Team) is fined €30,000 of which €20,000 is suspended for 12 months on condition that the Competitor does not commit a similar infringement during its pitstops in the meantime.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the team representative and reviewed video and in-car video evidence. During the pit stop of Car 27 (HUL), the automated release system initially displayed a green light after all four wheel guns had been removed from the wheel nuts and the respective mechanics had activated the release system. However, a mechanic was still in front of the car near the left-front wheel after having adjusted the front wing. The Team explained that its release procedure incorporates an additional manual safety check by a controller. When the responsible team member observed that the mechanic was still in front of the left-front wheel, the release signal was immediately changed back to red. HUL initially began to move away from the pit stop position in response to the green light. However, he immediately recognised that the light went back to red as the mechanic was still in front of the car and reacted promptly by stopping the car before it had fully left the pit stop position. The Stewards considered whether the initial green signal itself constituted an unsafe release. Article B1.6.2 defines when a car is deemed to have been released from its Designated Pit Stop Position. The relevant point is when the rear axle has passed the position previously occupied by the front axle while the car was stationary in its Designated Pit Stop Position. Accordingly, although the initial green signal was given prematurely and created an unsafe situation, the car was not “released” within the meaning of Article B1.6.2 while that situation existed. The Stewards therefore determine that no unsafe release occurred. In this case, although the initial green signal was given prematurely, the Team's backup safety procedure operated as intended and the signal was returned to red before the car had been released from its pit stop position. Nevertheless, the automatic premature green signal created an unsafe situation. While the Stewards determine that the circumstances did not constitute an unsafe release, the premature green signal nevertheless created an unsafe situation involving a team mechanic. The Stewards therefore impose a fine of €30,000 on the Competitor, of which €20,000 is suspended for the remainder of the 2026 season, subject to there being no further similar infringement. The substantial suspended element is intended to encourage the Competitor to review and, where necessary, improve its release procedures so as to prevent a recurrence of such an unsafe situation.

documents.title: Doc 57 - Decision - Car 23 - Alleged driving erratically
documents.subject: Decision - Car 23 - Alleged driving erratically

details.fact: Driving erratically in the pit entry road.
details.infringement: Alleged breaches of Article 1.8.5 of the FIA F1 Regulations and Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 e) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 23 (Alexander Albon), the driver of Car 81 (Oscar Piastri), the team representatives and reviewed video, in-car video and telemetry. On the approach to the pit entry, ALB reduced his speed, causing PIA, who was following closely behind, to brake and take avoiding action. No collision or contact occurred. ALB explained that immediately before entering the pit entry road he became aware that he was below the required delta time and therefore reduced his speed in order to comply with the applicable delta requirement. PIA confirmed, having heard ALB's explanation, that he considered the reason for ALB's actions understandable. While the situation required a significant reaction from PIA and could potentially have developed into a dangerous situation, the Stewards were satisfied that ALB's actions were taken in an attempt to comply with the applicable delta requirements and explained the otherwise unusual reduction in speed at that location. His actions, therefore, did not constitute erratic or unnecessarily dangerous driving in the circumstances. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determine that no infringement occurred and accordingly take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 52 - Infringement - Car 5 - Causing a collision with Car 55
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 5 - Causing a collision with Car 55

details.fact: Car 5 caused a collision with Car 55 in Turn 2.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed video and in-car video evidence. BOR attempted to overtake SAI on the inside of Turn 2. BOR did not have his front axle alongside SAI's mirror prior to the apex. Although he was close to the required position at the apex, BOR did not maintain the inside line and moved towards SAI, who had left sufficient space. Contact then occurred between BOR's right front tyre and the left side of SAI's car. The Stewards considered that BOR was not in full control of the overtaking manoeuvre and was wholly to blame for the collision. The Stewards note that the incident occurred shortly after the restart. However, the circumstances normally associated with a “first-lap” (restart) incident were not present. The Stewards therefore did not consider it appropriate to apply the more lenient approach normally taken to “first-lap” (restart) incidents. Accordingly, the Stewards determine that BOR caused the collision and impose the standard penalty.

documents.title: Doc 41 - Infringement - Car 18 - Failure to follow Race Director's instructions (SC2-SC1 Time) (2nd Offence)
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 18 - Failure to follow Race Director's instructions (SC2-SC1 Time) (2nd Offence)

details.fact: Car 18 exceeded the 1:59.0 time limit between the Safety Car lines.
details.infringement: Breach of Article B1.8.5 of the FIA F1 Regulations and Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code (non-compliance with the Race Director’s Competition Notes, item 1, document 33).
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the Driver of Car 18 (Lance Stroll), the team representative and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, timing, telemetry and in-car video evidence. Car 18 exceeded the maximum permitted SC2–SC1 time during Qualifying at 16:38:55. The driver and team explained that the configuration of the Power Unit requires a specific driving procedure during the out-laps. At this circuit, this made it particularly demanding for the Driver to manage his out-lap while at the same time meeting the prescribed SC2–SC1 time as accurately as possible. However, it does not relieve either the Driver or the Competitor of the obligation to comply with the prescribed maximum time. The Driver and Competitor remain responsible for operating the car, including its technical configuration, in a manner which enables compliance with the applicable regulations and the Race Director's instructions. The Stewards also note that STR was able to comply with the prescribed SC2–SC1 time on at least one other out-lap during the same Qualifying session while operating under the same general operational requirements. The Stewards therefore did not consider that the Power Unit configuration made compliance impossible. Having considered the circumstances of the incident, the Stewards determine that the exceedance constitutes an infringement. Taking into account all of the above, and in particular that compliance with the prescribed time remained possible, the Stewards determine that the standard sanction of a Warning is appropriate.

documents.title: Doc 26 - Infringement - Car 44 - Impeding of Car 5
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 44 - Impeding of Car 5

details.fact: Car 44 unnecessarily impeded Car 5 on the entry to Turn 9.
details.infringement: Breach of Article B4.1.1 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: Driver: Warning. The competitor (Scuderia Ferrari HP) is fined €10,000.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 44 (Lewis Hamilton), the driver of Car 5 (Gabriel Bortoleto), the team representatives and reviewed video, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence. HAM was travelling slowly approaching Turn 9 at approximately 80-85 km/h when BOR, who was on an out lap and not on a push lap, approached from behind at approximately 240 km/h, resulting in a closing speed of approximately 155-160 km/h. HAM moved from the middle of the track towards the racing line, at the end of the straight causing BOR to brake and take evasive action. The Stewards accept that HAM's right-hand mirror was damaged, as confirmed by photographic and video evidence, and that he had received no radio warning from the team. Both team representatives stated that such warnings are not normally issued where the approaching car is not on a push lap. BOR also confirmed that he remained in control of the situation. Nevertheless, the Stewards considered that HAM unnecessarily impeded the significantly faster approaching car by moving onto the racing line at slow speed. The fact that BOR was not on a push lap does not alter that conclusion. The Stewards also considered whether the incident should be regarded as dangerous impeding. In particular, they considered the high closing speed as well as the fact that a driver, who is aware that one of his mirrors is damaged, should exercise additional care before moving onto the racing line. However, BOR remained in control and was able to avoid HAM. The Stewards considered the damaged mirror and the fact that BOR was not on a push lap as mitigating circumstances. These were balanced against the significant speed differential, HAM's movement onto the racing line and the resulting need for BOR to take evasive action. Taking all the above into account, the Stewards determine that the standard penalty for impeding during a Practice session, which is a Warning, is appropriate. The Stewards also considered the responsibility of Scuderia Ferrari HP in relation to this incident. The Team was aware that HAM's right-hand mirror was damaged. As such, the Stewards determine that the Team should have provided appropriate radio warnings of significantly faster approaching cars, irrespective of whether those cars were on a push lap or not. The Stewards therefore determine that the Team failed to provide its driver with appropriate information in circumstances where it knew that his ability to observe approaching traffic was materially impaired by the damaged mirror and impose a fine of €10,000 on Scuderia Ferrari HP.
